projects.name: Custodian Labs · Guardian Layer
projects.summary: Used a 250-query ASQ-PHI subset to compare downstream detection before and after surrogate replacement, within a seven-benchmark study. This tests detectability of replaced identifiers, a proxy for utility.
projects.methodology: Latest v5 ASQ endpoint includes 534 replaced spans. Label-agnostic overlap recall across the detector panel is 91.9% before versus 91.1% after replacement; paired change −0.81 percentage points, 90% document-cluster bootstrap interval −1.37 to −0.26.
caveats: Only the replaced population is tested; replacement covers 80.9% of ASQ gold identifiers.
Gemma 4 31B transformed ASQ run covers 101/250 documents.
v2 corrected v1 span alignment and statistics; v1 explanations of truncation and redaction were withdrawn. Use v5 for current numerical claims.
Authors are affiliated with the transform's developer. No independent replication performed in this audit.

projects.name: University of Antwerp / UZA · MedDeID
projects.owner: University of Antwerp; Antwerp University Hospital
projects.summary: Evaluated a separately trained synthetic-English de-identifier on all 1,051 ASQ-PHI queries as an external portability benchmark, alongside six comparators.
projects.methodology: All 2,973 annotations were converted to character offsets; one required apostrophe normalization. Label-agnostic annotation-character recall was 98.90% (95% document-cluster interval 98.59–99.19). Raw non-PII character redaction was 6.21%; an age-exclusion sensitivity yielded 0.89%.
caveats: English training and testing were synthetic; ASQ results do not establish real-English clinical performance.
The age-exclusion sensitivity removes redactions over unannotated numeric ages while retaining the original non-PII denominator; it changes the endpoint.
Character recall is not exact entity recall, and character over-redaction is not a hard-negative query false-positive rate.
Shared post-processing and differing taxonomies affect comparisons; do not combine scores into a cross-study leaderboard.

projects.name: Oracle Health AI · AegisVox
projects.summary: Used all 1,051 ASQ-PHI queries for an independent text-detector evaluation within a long-form speech privacy study. This is a text benchmark use, separate from its 390-conversation audio experiments.
projects.methodology: Primary exact typed F1 is 94.4% over 2,147 contract-intersection gold elements. Full-ontology exact typed F1 is 79.9% over 2,973 elements; boundary-tolerant full-ontology F1 is 87.3%. Predictions occur in 48/219 hard-negative queries.
caveats: The primary endpoint excludes ontology categories outside the frozen detector contract; both primary and full-ontology results must be shown together.
Facility/organization geography and literal-year annotation disagreements affect scoring.
Text detection scores do not estimate identifier recall in speech or end-to-end audio privacy and cannot be multiplied by replacement realization.
This is research evidence, not proof of Oracle product deployment, certification or endorsement.

projects.name: HANK Safe Harbor
projects.summary: Uses all 1,051 ASQ-PHI queries as an external benchmark for a local two-encoder detect-and-replace pipeline.
projects.methodology: RoBERTa-large and XLM-R-large union plus structural detectors and consistent fake replacement. Reports recall 0.966 on 832 PHI-positive queries and hard-negative over-redaction 2.3% (5/219).
caveats: Author-reported results; this audit did not rerun inference.
AWS baseline is copied from ASQ-PHI authors, not rerun.
ASQ-PHI recall is not interchangeable with character-level recall reported by other projects.
Card discloses ages including 90+ are not treated as PHI; this differs from Safe Harbor.
One adoption family: do not count weight formats or related model cards as separate users.
The Hugging Face card is accessible; its linked GitHub repository returned 404 during this audit, limiting independent harness review.
projects.sourceReview: Full linked primary document and relevant implementation/protocol files read; no inference rerun.

display.oneLine: Reports evaluation of a local detection-and-replacement pipeline on all 1,051 queries.

projects.name: Outis
projects.summary: Benchmarks Outis, MedDeID and GLiNER on all 1,051 queries; explicitly labels ASQ-PHI as development evidence.
projects.methodology: DeBERTa-v3-base BIOES detector. Policy-aligned, label-agnostic ASQ scores: PHI characters masked 99.94%, non-PHI removed 0.18%, fully masked PHI documents 99.52%. Corpus/prediction hashes and pinned models are documented.
caveats: Failures were inspected during development, so ASQ-PHI is not an independent test.
Headline numbers use policy alignment; exact spans, original gold and adjusted scoring give different results.
Benchmarks README says evaluation-only while explicitly acknowledging development exposure.
PyPI, GitHub and Hugging Face describe one project, deduplicated here.
projects.quote: Development evidence means failures on that benchmark have been inspected, so it is no longer an independent test.

projects.name: Inkguard
projects.summary: Uses ASQ-PHI to develop and evaluate a local document-redaction tool, with explicit odd/even tuning and held-out halves.
projects.methodology: Reports 97.1% identifiers removed on the odd half, 96.8% on the even tuning half; 8 of 219 hard negatives changed. Measures software before human review.
caveats: Only the odd half is described as never used for tuning.
Results are author-reported and were not independently rerun.
Synthetic query benchmark does not validate real clinical records.
Scorer was corrected on 18 October; results depend on its alignment and identifier policy.
Evaluation date is reported as 18 October; publicly visible initial repository commit is 20 October 2026.

projects.name: Korean Step 4 PII candidate dataset
projects.summary: Credits ASQ-PHI’s question, record and memo-style variety as inspiration for a 10,000-example Korean PII candidate-classification dataset.
projects.methodology: 1,000 synthetic profiles × 10 tags; 8,000 train /1,000 validation /1,000 test. Designed for Qwen supervised tuning after an upstream NER stage; source-reference metadata points to 1,051 ASQ-PHI queries.
caveats: This documents adaptation of the dataset-construction approach; direct reuse of ASQ-PHI records for training or evaluation was not established.
Validation and test share generation frames and phrase components with training; card limits them to in-domain diagnostics.
Related Qwen model is downstream of this dataset, not a separate independently verified ASQ-PHI adoption.
